name: Lebanese Hashweh (Spiced Beef and Rice)
intro_html: Hashweh is the Lebanese answer to comfort food: cinnamon and allspice scented beef folded into buttery rice with toasted noodles. Simple ingredients, big warm flavor. Each bowl brings 25 grams of protein for about $2.95 (at everyday cost), and the whole thing cooks in one pot with about six real ingredients.
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Pantry seasonings (salt, black pepper, ground cinnamon, ground allspice): ~$3.05. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $24.58 across 14 servings, so roughly $1.76 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $30.91 across 14 servings, roughly $2.21 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $7.45 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $38.36. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About $2.95 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a dish a Middle Eastern restaurant would plate for $14. This is a genuinely cheap full dinner, and nobody eating it would ever guess.
shop_smart: Rice bought in the big bag runs about a third the price of the small boxes. This recipe uses 6.25 cups dry, and the big bag still keeps going for future batches.
The ground beef is over half the batch cost, so watch the weekly board. When 93/7 dips on sale, this gets even cheaper.
You do not need a vermicelli specialty pack. A few ounces of regular spaghetti snapped into inch-long pieces does the exact same job for pennies.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Melt about a third of the butter in your big pot and toast the broken spaghetti pieces, stirring, until deep golden. Watch it, they go from golden to burnt fast.
Add the rinsed rice and stir a minute to coat, then pour in the chicken broth. Bring to a boil, cover, drop to low, and cook about 15 minutes until tender. Rest 10 minutes off heat.
Meanwhile, brown the ground beef with the diced onion in a skillet with the remaining butter until no pink remains. Drain if needed.
Season the beef generously with cinnamon, allspice, salt, and pepper, and cook 2 more minutes so the spices bloom.
Fold the spiced beef into the rice gently with a fork so the grains stay fluffy.
Taste and adjust salt. Traditional move: top with extra toasted nuts if you have them on hand.
portion_html: Weigh the full pot, subtract the empty pot number you wrote down in step 1, and divide by 14. Scoop that weight into each container and you get 14 even bowls at 577 calories and 25 grams of protein apiece.
credit_html: Recipe adapted from Silk Road Recipes, rebuilt for 14-serving budget meal prep with weighed portions and Omaha pricing.
upsell_html: Hearty dinners for about $2.95 a bowl (at everyday cost). This is one of many. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons, calculators, and tools, all for $1 a month.

head.description: Lebanese hashweh meal prep: 577 calories and 25g protein at about $2.95 a bowl (at everyday cost). Cinnamon and allspice beef with buttery rice, 14 one-pot servings.
head.keywords: lebanese hashweh recipe, spiced beef and rice, middle eastern meal prep, budget one pot dinner, cheap ground beef recipe, hashweh rice
steps: Toast broken spaghetti in butter until golden.
Add rice and chicken broth, cover, and simmer about 15 minutes until tender.
Brown ground beef with onion in the remaining butter, then season with cinnamon, allspice, salt, and pepper.
Fold the spiced beef into the rice with a fork.
